# Drugs, addiction and terror

## In short
- Your first drug of the day gives you the **Drugged** status. A second drug on the same day makes you **Hooked!** (addicted) for good. From then on, if you start a night as an addict without being Drugged, you die of addiction [1] [2] [3].
- Anabolic Steroids raise your AP to your maximum (6, or 5 when wounded). Twinoid raises it to max + 2. Betapropine raises it to max + 20 and does not count as a drug. LSD, Unlabelled Drug and expired Betapropine have random results, including terror and addiction [4] [5] [6] [7].
- **Terrorised** lasts until you cure it, because it is not cleared at night. While terrorised you cannot make a desperate escape or explore ruins, and moving out of a zone with zombies fails 5% of the time. On night watch you lose 30 defence and get +5% death chance [8] [9].
- Cures for terror: Valium Shot, Cigarettes with Matches, Pocket Vibrator, Teddy Bear (30%), expired Betapropine (25%) and a shaman's healing (65%). To stop terror before it happens, keep a Little Book of Calm in your rucksack, or in your home chest while you are in town [10] [11] [7].

## How it works

### Taking drugs
- Most drug items have two versions of their action. Version `_1` needs requirement `drug_1` and gives **Drugged** (`drug_any`). Version `_2` needs `status_drugged=true` and gives **Addict** (`drug_addict`), with the message "you must now take a drug every day… or DIE" [4].
- Drugged is volatile, so it is removed at the start of each new day [1] [12]. Addict is not volatile [2].
- When you get Drugged or Addict, you lose the **Clean** status ("You have never taken drugs") [7] [13].
- **How AP effects work:** a "relative to max" effect sets your AP to max(current AP, max AP + value). Your current AP is never lowered. Max AP is 6, or 5 when wounded [7].

### Drug effects

| Item | Effect |
|---|---|
| Anabolic Steroids | AP up to max + 0 (6 AP) [4] |
| Twinoid 500mg | AP up to max + 2 (8 AP) [5] |
| Betapropine 5mg | AP up to max + 20 (26 AP) and status `tg_betadrug`. It only needs `not_yet_beta` and does **not** give Drugged or Addict [6] |
| Hydratone 100mg | Gives Drugged or Addict. If you are Thirsty, it also removes Thirsty [14] |
| Paracetoid 7g | Gives **Immunised**. If you are infected, it also cures the infection. The in-game message says the protection ends after the attack [15] |
| Valium Shot | If you are terrorised, it removes terror. You can also take it when not terrorised, and it then only counts as a drug [10] |
| LSD | 75%: 6 AP. 25%: 6 AP **and terror** [16] |
| Unlabelled Drug | 40%: drugged + 6 AP. 20%: drugged + terror. 20%: **addict** + `just_ap7`. 20%: no effect. If you are already drugged, every outcome except "no effect" makes you addicted [17] |
| Betapropine 5mg (expired) | 25% each: 6 AP, cures terror, +4 AP, drunk. Gives drugged, or addict if you are already drugged [18] |
| Black Neck Ooze (April Fools only) | AP up to max + 2 and `tg_april_ooze` [19]. At the new day this gives infection and paranoia [12] |
| Christmas candy (food) | Uses the `plus_ap8_30` effect. Then 18% addict, 50% terror, 30% infection, 2% death by poison [20] |
| Cyanide | Kills you. You can use it from day 2 [21] |

- **Food with "strange" poison:** eating it has a 50% chance of a random effect. In 1 case out of 4, you become drugged, or addicted if you were already drugged. In the other 3 cases, you become drunk.

### Addiction
- Addiction is checked in the status-death stage, before the attack. A living citizen who has `addict` but not `drugged` dies with cause Addiction, and the body does not come back as a zombie [3].
- This check runs before the new day clears volatile statuses. So a drug taken during the day keeps you alive that night [3] [12].
- **Night watch:** Hooked! adds +6% death chance and +10 watch defence. Drugged adds +10 watch defence. Status values add up, so an addict who took a drug today gets +20 defence [2] [1] [22].
- None of the documents I read contain an item or action that removes addiction.

### Getting terrorised
1. **Night attack, at home.** This applies to a citizen who is attacked and survives. The chance in % starts at 100 [3], minus:
   - your decoration points (at most 10)
   - 3 if you have `tg_clothes` or carry a Town Uniform
   - 5 for `tg_home_clean`
   - 10 for `tg_home_shower`
   - 25 for `good_smell`
   - 10 for Earplugs (`bquies_#00`) in your rucksack or chest

   Citizens who are already terrorised are skipped. The cinema exception is turned off in the code (`$has_kino = false`) [3].
2. **Night watch.**
   - c = 8% + a fatigue value that depends on how many times you have watched before. Wound chance = 1 − ((1−c) − (1−c)·0.2). Terror chance = 1 − ((1−c) − (1−c)·0.1) [22].
   - Modifiers: `good_smell` sets terror to 0. The Gas Gun adds +10% terror. `tg_home_shower` gives −2.5% [22].
   - A watcher who survives on a night when zombies get in is hit with chance wound + terror. Whether it is a wound or terror is picked in proportion to the two chances. The **Small Trebuchet** blocks terror from the watch [3] [23].
3. **Items:**
   - Cursed Cuddly Toy: always gives terror [24].
   - LSD, Unlabelled Drug and Christmas candy can give terror (see the table above).
   - Halloween: 50% chance of terror at the new day if you keep a `haunting_soul` in your chest [3].
- **Prevention:** unless the effect is forced, terror is blocked if you have a `prevent_terror` item (Little Book of Calm) in your rucksack, or also in your home chest when you are in town [7] [11].

### What terror does
- **Desperate escape:** refused while you are terrorised [9].
- **Ruin exploration:** blocked while you are terrorised [9].
- **Moving:** when you leave a zone with zombies, there is a 5% chance your move fails and you lose 1 AP. Terrorised escorted citizens also have this 5% chance, and if one fails the whole group does not move [9].
- **Night watch:** −30 defence and +5% death chance [8].
- **Shaman healing:** a terrorised shaman cannot heal others [25].

### Curing terror
- **Valium Shot:** always works, but counts as a drug (drugged, or addicted if already drugged) [10].
- **Opened packet of Cigarettes:** needs a Box of Matches and terror. It always cures terror. The matches are used up 66% of the time and the packet 33% of the time [26].
- **Pocket Vibrator:** in town only. It cures terror and the item becomes empty [27].
- **Teddy Bear:** 30% chance to cure, once per day (`tg_teddy`) [28].
- **Betapropine (expired):** 25% chance to cure [18].
- **Shaman healing:**
  - Cost: 2 MP for the shaman role, or 2 AP for the shaman job. The cost is paid even if the healing fails.
  - The patient must be in town and can be healed only once per day.
  - The game picks one status at random among the patient's terror, infection, drunk and drugged, and removes it with a 65% chance.
  - When it works, there is a 5% chance the healed status passes to the healer [25].
  - ⚠️ Warning: this can remove **Drugged**. If that happens to an addict who cannot take another drug that day, they die of addiction that night [25] [3].

## What changes it
- **Cheat Death (`hsurvive`):** protects you from all status deaths, including addiction [3].
- **`hsurvive2`:** protects you only if your `HeroImmuneStatusList` contains `addiction`. **`hsurvive3`** only covers thirst and infection [3].
- **Statuses** `good_smell`, `tg_home_shower`, `tg_home_clean` and `tg_clothes`, and the items Earplugs and Town Uniform, lower your terror chance (see above) [3].
- **Buildings:** Small Trebuchet blocks terror from the watch. Gas Gun adds +10% terror on the watch [3] [22].
- **`tg_stats_locked`:** blocks all status changes, including drugs and terror [7].

## Town types
- **Pandemonium (panda):** the terror ratio on the watch is 0.2 instead of 0.1, and the wound ratio is 0.3 instead of 0.2 [22]. With c = 8%, terror is about 26% instead of about 17%.
- **Default, small, remote and custom:** I found no other differences for drugs, addiction or terror.

## Not verified
- I did not read the exact conditions of requirement `drug_1`. It is assumed to mean "not yet drugged".
- The second point effect of the drugs (`pointType=4`, "relative to extension max") was not traced to a point type.
- These effect atoms were not read: `just_ap7`, `plus_4ap`, `plus_ap8_30`.
- The default contents of `HeroImmuneStatusList` were not read.
- The shaman check looks for a status named `infected`, while the infection status is called `infection`. So an infected shaman may still be allowed to heal. This was not tested.
- These come only from summaries, not from code I read:
  - Playing cards: 1/54 chance of terror.
  - Guitar: +2 AP for drunk, drugged or addicted citizens in town.
